title: It's Super Busy!!
letter:
Hey everybody, how's it going?

It's my first P-Day and it's only Friday. It's the first week so it's super nice, super convenient. I've heard Friday is the best day, so it's super sweet.

Today you get two hours of exercise on P-Day so we went up and we played sand volleyball, spikeball, we went to the courts, played pickleball, and it's super awesome. And in the gym they count everything as sight and sound.

And just so you know what that means, you always have to be within sight and sound of your companion. Like literally if your companion turns away and is talking to someone else, you can no longer hear them. That is outside of sound. So you have to be that close and attached to them, but in the gym they allow it, so someone could be running, someone could be exercising and you could be on the main courts, which is super nice.

The campus is pretty sick and pretty big and pretty easy to navigate, which is saying something from someone who usually doesn't know directions. I'm definitely learning and I'm hoping to get better, so we'll see. I can hear my dad laughing at this.

But yeah, it's been so awesome. It's such a spiritual time and it's really incredible. It's such a blast getting to know the guys, getting to know the Hermanas. Yeah, I'm trying not to say guys anymore, they want us to say, "Oh those are the Hermanas." Just getting to know everyone, getting a sense of independence is awesome and it's super fun.

You are definitely busy. There's not a ton of free time, that's for sure. You will be very busy, non-stop moving. But you get some free time and a lot of it's really up to you. Like you don't have to do personal study. You don't have to do anything. But at the same time you're going to lose a lot if you don't. So really you should be doing it. And those times are really great.

They have the basic structure of the day, it's the typical. You know you study in the morning. You have lunch and breakfast and then in the afternoon, at least for me, it can change per person. You go to a class and you have some time and then you go to dinner. Sometimes there's a devotional from a General Authority and all you do is you just make sure you wear a suit. If you're not wearing a suit, you should be. But if it's anything else you don't need to be wearing a suit.

Our dorms are all in this nice collected area and it's super fun. People have a blast in the dorms. It is definitely like a dichotomy watching people honestly because you'll see some boys do some very questionable things and then they'll be called as district leader. Which is, you know, as you can imagine, there are districts and they're just in charge of our area and some of them, I'll tell you, I don't agree with at all. But at the same time I'm like, hey, the Lord called them so I'm going to trust that and I'm just going to give up my prejudices and just kind of listen. So I think that's important to remember for sure.

When at the MTC, just like the things I'm noticing is you really gotta swallow your pride. You gotta swallow the disobedience. And to be honest that sounds like some propaganda poster, you know, like "you must be obedient." But I kind of thought of it at least the way it made sense to me, it's like if I said, hey here's a workout that will get you in amazing shape and you have to have a strict diet and you have to have these strict rules and then you're going to get in amazing shape and do what you want.

And so I take that as the same principle and that's how I remember it because someone like me, I hate being told what to do, but if the Savior's telling it then you know it's good to listen up, it's the best thing to listen up. I will say sometimes they make me really mad, that's for sure. Like we just picked the district leaders and we all were like, hey congrats, you know, they just walked in the room and then the guy said, alright I know you're all cheering and you know what we'll work on that, and we were just dead silent because he was so serious. He was talking about how irreverent we were for celebrating that and I was like, okay. And you know this side of me that doesn't like to listen to people got mad, but I think it's natural and swallowing my pride is just part of the game, especially for me.

But yeah, it's such a great time. I wanted to bear my testimony on the gift of tongues most importantly. What came to my mind is just like the more you apply it, the more you rely on the Lord, the more you turn to Him, you pray to Him and you just talk with Him about it, the more you'll improve and you just apply it everywhere. You walk outside your room, you start trying to speak Spanish and the biggest thing for me that I've really been trying to work on is I signed up to learn Spanish because I want to learn it, but that was a bit selfish to be honest, because really it's not about me, it's about these people that I can go serve. So I'm learning to just give it up for them and to say like, hey you know what, I'm so blessed. There are some families I need to teach in Spanish and they just don't have it as good, they need this gospel and I need to push past that. And I think that will even help me go further because I'll know that I'm pushing not for me but for the hundreds, maybe even thousands of people that I will proselyte to on my mission and reach out to.

So I bear my testimony that if you continue to strengthen your skills and your efforts and dedicate them to the Lord and most importantly to others beyond just yourself, you'll be blessed and the Lord will help you get there.

I say these things in the name of Jesus Christ, amen.

It's been awesome and I hope you guys have an amazing week. See you!

*- Élder Bundy*

P.S

Forgot to say that my district is awesome with great missionaries and we went to the temple today which is always such a blessing! My companion is goated!
